conviction_note: The main lean is that management used the identical words for Q2 ('net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower year over year') that it used for Q1, when Q1 then came in flat year over year against a consensus cut about 25%. Q2 consensus of $0.63 is cut 36% from last year's $0.98 and sits only about 10% above Q1's $0.57, while Q2 has historically run well above Q1. Kalwall adds two months of a 15%-EBITDA business. The stock has paid for beats only when the guide held (+15.2% in June 2026, -4.4% in October 2025 on a beat with a cut guide). So the aluminum and tariff overhang on the guide and a weak ABI hold p_up at 60 rather than higher. abs_move 11 sits between the 9.7% event-implied move and the 12.7% median reaction, with a guide update likely because two acquisitions closed. (2*0.60-1)*11 = +2.2, against an impact_sum of +3.4. The gap is the guide risk the findings do not size.
bar: Adj EPS $0.63, from two agreeing sources: MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-apogee-enterprises-apog-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/ and TradingView https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:74b9b23617b40:0-apog-q2-26-earnings-revenue-estimate-is-359-46m-usd/. Revenue is disputed: $359.5m on MarketBeat and TradingView, but StockStory (2026-10-05) has -1.9% y/y, about $351m (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/apog/news/earnings/apogee-apog-reports-earnings-tomorrow-what-to-expect-2). The company's own Q2 guide is qualitative: 'net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower on a year over year basis' against Q2 FY26 sales $358m and adj EPS $0.98 (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). FY27 guide: adj EPS $2.70-3.25, sales $1.43-1.48bn including Kalwall (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000058/a53026fy27q1results.htm). FY consensus is about $3.00, the midpoint. print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS, assuming about $0.75.
positioning_check: Short interest 935,284 shares, 4.63% of float, 4.48 days to cover, up from 840,316 the month before (stockanalysis.com, read 2026-10-05, settlement date not shown; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/apog/statistics/). Not crowded. The 25-delta skew is +0.99 vol points, which is balanced, and put/call OI is 0.78 on only 272 contracts, so the options market makes no directional statement. Run-up is -9.46% over 20 days and -26% from the 52-week high. The stock gave back the whole +15% Q1 reaction, from about $42 on 2026-06-24 (the director grant price) to $36.19, and is down 8.1% over the month against -3.3% for peers (StockStory, 2026-10-05). The price is leaning negative into the print, not positive.

findings.finding: The CFO's Q2 guide on 2026-06-26 is word for word the guide he gave for Q1 on 2026-04-24 ('net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower on a year over year basis'). Q1 then printed sales -1.1% and adj EPS $0.57 against $0.55 a year earlier, flat, versus a $0.41-0.43 consensus. 'Q1 profit exceeded our internal expectations', and pricing and surcharges put in during Q1 'benefit results through the remainder of the fiscal year'. The Q2 consensus of $0.63 is 36% below last year's $0.98 and only about 10% above Q1's $0.57. Last year Q2 ran 78% above Q1 ($0.98 against about $0.55, from the FY26 total of $3.47 less Q2-Q4). The bar looks set at the bottom of what 'lower' allows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26) beat EPS by about 35% with the guide held: +15.16%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09) beat ($0.98 vs $0.86) with the FY guide lowered: -4.44%. Q3 FY26 (2026-01-07) missed with the guide cut: -13.89%. Beats pay only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus did not move after the Q1 beat ($0.63 still a 36% y/y decline), and the stock has fallen about 14% since the Q1 reaction, to below the pre-print level. If the market expected another beat, the stock would not have round-tripped the June move, and the street number would sit nearer Q2's usual seasonal step-up. On 2-4 analysts, the bar is the mechanical result of applying 'lower' to the guide's midpoint.
findings.independence: Same management language in a different document, the Q4 FY26 call of 2026-04-24 (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/24/apogee-apog-q4-2026-earnings-transcript/). Q1 actuals are in the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000058/a53026fy27q1results.htm). Year-ago $0.98 is in the Q2 FY26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684525000154/a83025fy26q2results.htm). The 'beat 100% of the time over 2 years' figure comes from StockStory. All of this is one inference about guide conservatism, not a number from the quarter.

findings.finding: Kalwall closed 2026-07-01 ($105m cash plus up to $10m earnout), so it carries two months of Q2 (Jul-Aug). Management sized it at about $85m revenue in the first 12 months at about 15% EBITDA, roughly $14m of revenue and $2m of EBITDA in Q2. Organic 'slightly lower' than $358m (about $350m) plus Kalwall implies about $362-366m. That is above both the $359.5m and the about $351m (-1.9% y/y) consensus figures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue moved the stock less than EPS and the guide. Q1 FY27 revenue beat ($342.7m vs about $334m) came alongside the EPS beat at +15%. Q2 FY26 revenue beat ($358m vs $334m) still fell 4.4% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The two revenue consensus figures disagree by about $8m, and the lower one (-1.9% y/y) reads as if Kalwall is excluded. Management called Q2 Kalwall impact 'minimal', which may have kept it out of models. If it were priced, both sources would sit at or above $362m.
findings.independence: Kalwall revenue and margin figures are from the Q1 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). That shares a document with finding 1 but rests on a different fact. Capped small because the revenue bar is disputed.

findings.finding: GroGlass was announced 2026-09-02 and closed 2026-09-18: about EUR62.5m (about $72m) including up to EUR10m earnout, about $30m of first-12-month revenue at about 25% adj EBITDA, funded from cash and the revolver. The company said it 'will discuss additional strategic and financial details during its second quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call', so the FY27 guide will very likely be restated to include it. That adds about $12-15m of FY27 sales at a margin above the group's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Kalwall was folded into the guide in June 2026, the sales range rose $50m with EPS unchanged, and the stock rose 15% on the quarter. The acquisition line has no separate reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but no accretion or guide figure has been given. The stock fell after the announcement (about $37.9 on 2026-09-11 to $36.2), which does not look like a market crediting accretion. The financing question has an answer: the money buys a 25%-margin coatings business, and leverage was 1.3x at Q1 with $419m of revolver capacity, so this is not a distress read.
findings.independence: Closing release reported by Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/apogee-enterprises-completes-groglass-acquisition-for-718m-93CH-4907842). Liquidity is from the Q1 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000063/apog-20260530.htm).

findings.finding: Direct peer Tecnoglass reported on 2026-08-06 that the all-in US aluminum price was up about 77% y/y, cut its gross margin to 37.3% from 44.7%, and narrowed FY26 guidance on 'sustained high aluminum costs'. It said commercial pricing passes through slowly: late 2026 for small projects, late 2027 for large ones. Apogee's Architectural Services runs long fixed-price contracts, and its margin was already 5.3% in Q1 against 7.5% in Q4 and 9.7% in Q3. LME stayed at about $3,270/t through August 2026, so the cost pressure persisted through Apogee's Q2 and is the main risk to the guide holding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Apogee fell 13.89% on 2026-01-07 when it cut the FY26 guide on a tariff and aluminum drag of about $0.30. Aluminum and tariffs are the line that has produced its largest down moves.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer's print landing after Apogee last spoke (2026-06-26). Apogee's FY guide has not been revisited since, and FY consensus sits at the $3.00 midpoint. It is partly priced: Apogee's 20-day run-up is -9.5% and it is underperforming peers.
findings.independence: LME August 2026 average of about $3,273/t (https://www.alcircle.com/news/lme-aluminium-price-rises-above-1-as-stocks-drop-to-246-825t-on-august-26-120941). Apogee's own April call cited aluminum +87% y/y (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/24/apogee-apog-q4-2026-earnings-transcript/). Tecnoglass is a proxy: Apogee has said its pricing and surcharges offset the cost, so this is filed small.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 the US signaled tariffs on some Canadian aluminum could drop to 25% from 50% under a tentative deal. The September Midwest premium fell 8.2% to 95c/lb and Oct/Nov contracts fell more than 12%. Apogee's FY26 guide cut blamed tariffs on Canadian aluminum. Offsetting this, a secondary source (2026-09-17) says Section 338 duties stacked onto Canadian aluminum bars, rods and tubes from 2026-09-15; another source says goods already under Section 232 were carved out. Net, a mild easing of the H2 input-cost outlook with real two-way uncertainty.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The tariff line drove the -13.89% January 2026 reaction. The CFO called FY26's $9m tariff impact 'a tailwind now in 27' (April 2026 call).
findings.why_not_priced: Macro news the stock has not visibly reacted to: it fell through late August and September. Management has not yet said whether forward premiums change its H2 cost view, and the call will be the first place it does.
findings.independence: Bloomberg 2026-08-20 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/aluminum-premium-slips-as-us-set-to-cut-tariffs-on-canada-metal). The contrary Section 338 stacking claim is at https://discoveryalert.com/analysis/us-canada-aluminum-tariffs-september-2026/, and the carve-out at https://www.tariffstool.com/guides/canada-tariff-50-percent-section-338-august-2026. This is macro-to-company transmission, unconfirmed by Apogee.

findings.finding: The AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index was 47.2 in August 2026 (46.6 in July), still contracting in what AIA calls the longest slump in the index's history, with weaker forward expectations (25% expect Q4 billings to rise, 29% to fall). The Dodge Momentum Index was flat at 282.0 in August, with commercial planning down 3.0%. This is a soft backdrop for Glass, where Q1 already showed 'softer conditions in new construction and lower demand for premium offerings', and for Metals volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Apogee's guide said results weight to H2 'reflecting anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions'. These series do not show that improvement yet.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is a public series and the slump is four years old. The incremental point is that management's H2 assumption of market improvement is not visible in the data, which could make the guide's top end harder to defend. Against this, Services backlog was $734.5m, up 8% y/y in Q1.
findings.independence: Dodge Momentum Index for August (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/09/08/dodge-momentum-index-slowed-in-august/). Against it: Tecnoglass's COO said US demand is 'surprisingly high everywhere' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-tecnoglass-q2-2026-revenue-hits-record-as-shares-fall-93CH-4843134). These are broad series, sized small.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive (a low bar on repeated guide language) against a price that has round-tripped the June beat and is down 9.5% over 20 days. The skew is flat at +0.99, so the options market does not contradict the lean. The cut has been in the price, not in the options, and the leaning negative into the print is what leaves room for a beat to pay.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): EPS $0.63 is confirmed by two agreeing sources, so the main finding stays at +3.5. Revenue consensus is disputed ($359.5m vs about $351m), so the Kalwall revenue finding is capped at +0.5 from +0.8.

Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): checked the reaction history on this line. Beats were bought only when the guide held, and a guide risk exists on aluminum. That kept p_up at 60 rather than raising it. The finding size is unchanged.
Rules 5 and 7: peer and macro items stay small. Short interest of 4.6% is not crowded, so the small negatives are not shrunk further. Nothing else changed.
